description:
## Goal

Give operators (and us) a cheap, always-on diagnostic that shows
exactly which subsystem is leaking. Without this, the next
multi-day investigation is the same as this one.

## Approach

1. In Monitoring.report_status (src/fetcher/monitoring.cr), add
   RSS deltas: capture rss_mb at startup, store in a class var,
   and log "RSS +X MB since startup" + "delta over last interval"
   on every report.
2. Extend the existing memory log line with: FiberTracker active
   count, EventBroadcaster client count, SocketManager
   connection count, StringIntern pool size, RateLimiter cache
   size, FaviconActor @client_pool size (need a new getter).
3. Add a "heap snapshot" trigger every N cycles (configurable,
   default 6) that writes /proc/<pid>/{maps,smaps,status} + GC.stats
   to /tmp/qh-snap-<ts>/. Wire it to the existing
   MemoryManagerActor.dump_heap(false) call (cheap, no gcore).
4. Log the rss_mb of the snapshot before/after to make it clear
   what GC reclaimed.

## Acceptance

- One new log line per reporter tick with all the counters and
  deltas.
- A snapshot directory is created every ~30 min and the path
  appears in the log.
- The log line includes FaviconActor @client_pool size, which
  requires adding a `client_pool_size` getter to FaviconActor.
- Build + spec + ameba clean.

## Note

MemoryManagerActor.dump_heap already exists from the earlier
investigation (quickhea-qm4). This task wires it into the
reporter loop.
title: Add periodic heap snapshot + RSS delta logging
